blocks.chantTranslation:
\V. Pray, Lord, give a blessing.
May the almighty Lord grant us a quiet night and a perfect end. \R. Amen.
Brethren, be sober and watchful;
because your adversary the devil,               as a roaring lion,
goes about seeking whom he may devour; resist him, steadfast in the faith.
\V. But you, O Lord, have mercy upon us.//\R. Thanks be to God.
\V. Our help is in the name of the Lord.//\R. Who made heaven and earth.

blocks.text:
Here all pause in silence wherein one may make a short examination of conscience or quietly say a Pater Noster.

The Officiant now bows profoundly and says the Confiteor alone in a low voice, recto tono. After this, all bow toward the Officiant and reply in the same low voice:
Misereátur tui omnípotens Deus, et dimíssis peccátis tuis, perdúcat te ad vitam ætérnam. \R. Amen.
blocks.translation: May almighty God have mercy on you, forgive you your sins, and bring you to everlasting life. \R. Amen

blocks.text: The Officiant stands upright, while everyone else, still standing, bows profoundly toward the Blessed Sacrament and says in a low voice:

Confíteor Deo omnipoténti, beátæ Maríæ semper Vírgini, beáto Michaéli Archángelo, beáto Joánni Baptístæ, sanctis Apóstolis Petro et Paulo, ómnibus Sanctis et tibi pater, quia peccávi nimis, cogitatióne, verbo et ópere: mea culpa, mea culpa, mea máxima culpa. Ideo precor beátam Maríam semper Vírginem, beátum Michaélem Archángelum, beátum Joánnem Baptístam, sanctos Apóstolos Petrum et Paulum, omnes Sanctos, et te pater: oráre pro me ad Dóminum Deum nostrum.
blocks.translation: I confess to almighty God, to blessed Mary ever Virgin, to blessed Michael the Archangel, to blessed John the Baptist, to the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and to all the Saints, that I have sinned exceedingly in thought, word and deed: strikes his breast through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault. Therefore I beseech blessed Mary ever Virgin, blessed Michael the Archangel, blessed John the Baptist, the holy Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints, to pray for me to the Lord our God.

blocks.text: Misereátur  vestri  omnípotens  Deus,  et  dimíssis  peccátis  vestris, perdúcat vos ad vitam ætérnam. \R. Amen.
blocks.translation: May almighty God have mercy on you, forgive you your sins, and bring you to everlasting life. \R. Amen

blocks.text: All stand upright and make the Sign of  the Cross as he continues:

Indulgéntiam, absolutiónem, et remissiónem peccatórum nostrórum tríbuat nobis omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
\R. Amen.
blocks.translation:
May the almighty and merciful Lord grant us pardon, absolution and remission of our sins.
\R. Amen.

blocks.text: All make the Sign of the Cross with their thumbs over their hearts, as the Officiant sings:

blocks.chantTranslation:
\V. Convert us, O God, our Saviour.//\R. And turn away your anger from us.
\V. O God, come to my assistance.//\R. O Lord, make haste to help me.

Glory be…
Have mercy on me, O Lord,//and hear my prayer.
_Ps. 4_  When I called,//the God of my justice heard me:
in my distress you gave me room.

blocks.text:
1. Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
  2. Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem et quǽritis mendácium?
  3. Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
  4. Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: † quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, * in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
  5. Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, † et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: quis osténdit nobis bona?
  6. Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
  7. A fructu fruménti, vini et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
  8. In pace in idípsum * dórmiam et requiéscam;
  9. Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
  10. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
  11. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.translation:
1. Have mercy on me, * and hear my prayer.
  2. O sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity and seek after falsehood?
  3. And know that the Lord has made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I cry to him.
  4. Be angry, and do not sin: † what you say in your hearts, * be contrite for upon your beds.
  5. Offer the sacrifice of righteousness, † and trust in the Lord. * Many say, "Who will show us good things?"
  6. The light of your countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * you have given gladness in my heart.
  7. More than when their grain, wine, and oil * increased abundantly,
  8. In peace, in the selfsame thing, * I will lie down and sleep;
  9. For you alone, O Lord, * have established me in hope and security.
  10. Glory be…

blocks.chantTranslation: _Ps. 90_  He who dwells in the help of the Most High, shall abide under the protection of the God of heaven.

blocks.text:
1. Dicet Dómino: Suscéptor meus es tu, et refúgium meum: * Deus meus sperábo in eum.
  2. Quóniam ipse liberávit me de láqueo venántium, * et a verbo áspero.
  3. Scápulis suis obumbrábit tibi: * et sub pennis eius sperábis.
  4. Scuto circúmdabit te véritas eius: * non timébis a timóre noctúrno.
  5. A sagítta volánte in die, † a negótio perambulánte in ténebris: * ab incúrsu et dæmónio meridiáno.
  6. Cadent a látere tuo mille, † et decem míllia a dextris tuis: * ad te autem non appropinquábit.
  7. Verúmtamen óculis tuis considerábis: * et retributiónem peccatórum vidébis.
  8. Quóniam tu es, Dómine, spes mea: * Altíssimum posuísti refúgium tuum.
  9. Non accédet ad te malum: * et flagéllum non appropinquábit tabernáculo tuo.
  10. Quóniam Angelis suis mandávit de te: * ut custódiant te in ómnibus viis tuis.
  11. In mánibus portábunt te: * ne forte offéndas ad lápidem pedem tuum.
  12. Super áspidem et basilíscum ambulábis: * et conculcábis leónem et dracónem.
  13. Quóniam in me sperávit, liberábo eum: * prótegam eum quóniam cognóvit nomen meum.
  14. Clamábit ad me, et ego exáudiam eum: † cum ipso sum in tribulatióne: * erípiam eum et glorificábo eum.
  15. Longitúdine diérum replébo eum: * et osténdam illi salutáre meum.
  16. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
  17. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.translation:
1. He shall say to the Lord: You are my protector and my refuge: * my God, in him I will trust.
  2. For he has delivered me from the snare of the hunters, * and from the grievous word.
  3. He will overshadow you with his shoulders, * and under his wings you shall trust.
  4. His truth shall surround you with a shield: * you shall not fear the terror of the night,
  5. Nor the arrow that flies by day, † nor the pestilence that walks in darkness: * nor the assault and the noonday demon.
  6. A thousand shall fall at your side, † and ten thousand at your right hand: * but it shall not come near you.
  7. Nevertheless, with your eyes you shall behold: * and see the punishment of sinners.
  8. For you, O Lord, are my hope: * you have made the Most High your refuge.
  9. No evil shall come upon you: * nor shall any scourge draw near your dwelling.
  10. For he has given his angels charge over you: * to guard you in all your ways.
  11. They shall bear you in their hands: * lest perhaps you strike your foot against a stone.
  12. You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk: * and you shall trample underfoot the lion and the dragon.
  13. Because he has hoped in me, I will deliver him: * I will protect him because he has known my name.
  14. He shall cry to me, and I will hear him: † I am with him in tribulation; * I will rescue him and glorify him.
  15. With length of days I will satisfy him: * and I will show him my salvation.
  16. Glory be…

blocks.chantTranslation: _Ps. 133_  Behold now, bless the Lord,//all you servants of the Lord;

blocks.text:
1. Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
  2. In nóctibus extóllite manus vestras in sancta, * et benedícite Dóminum.
  3. Benedícat te Dóminus ex Sion, * qui fecit cælum et terram.
  4. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
  5. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.translation:
1. Who stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.
  2. In the night lift up your hands to the holy place, * and bless the Lord.
  3. May the Lord bless you out of Sion, * he who made heaven and earth.
  4. Glory be…

blocks.chantTranslation: Have mercy on me, O Lord,//and hear my prayer.

Before the ending of the light,//we ask you, Creator of all things,
that in your mercy you//may be our protector and guardian.
Let dreams depart far away,//and the fantasies of the night;
and restrain our enemy,//lest our bodies be defiled.
Grant this, most loving Father, //and only Son, equal to the Father,
together with the Holy Spirit the Comforter, reigning for all eternity. Amen.

You, O Lord, are among us, and your holy name has been invoked upon us:
do not forsake us, O Lord our God.
\R. Thanks be to God.

\V. Into your hands, O Lord,//I commend my spirit.
\R. You have redeemed me,//O Lord, God of truth.
Glory be...

\V. Guard us, O Lord,//as the apple of your eye.
\R. And protect us under//the shadow of your wings.

Save us, O Lord, while awake;//guard us while we sleep,
that we may watch with Christ //and rest in peace.
Now you dismiss your servant, O Lord,//according to your word in peace:

blocks.text:
1. Quia vidérunt óculi mei * salutáre tuum,
  2. Quod parásti * ante fáciem ómnium populórum,
  3. Lumen ad revelatiónem Géntium, * et glóriam plebis tuæ Israël.
  4. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
  5. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
blocks.translation:
1. For my eyes have seen * your salvation,
  2. Which you have prepared * before the face of all peoples,
  3. A light for the revelation of the Gentiles, * and the glory of your people Israel.
  4. Glory be…

blocks.chantTranslation:
Save us, O Lord, while awake; //guard us while we sleep,
that we may watch with Christ //and rest in peace.

\V. The Lord be with you.
\R. And with your spirit.

\V. Let us bless the Lord.
\R. Thanks be to God.

blocks.text:
Thursday 9th July
Friday 10th July
Saturday 11th July
blocks.translation:
Pedro de Bermudez (1558–1605)
Cristóbal de Morales (c.1500–1553)
Fernando de las Infantas (1534–c.1610)

blocks.text: Salve, Regína, mater misericórdiæ; vita, dulcédo et spes nóstra, salve. Ad te clamámus éxsules fílii Hevæ. Ad te suspirámus geméntes et flentes In hac lacrimárum valle. Eia ergo, advocáta nostra, illos tuos misericórdes óculos ad nos convérte. Et Iesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui, nobis post hoc exsílium osténde. O clemens, O pia, O dulcis Virgo María.
blocks.translation: Hail, Queen, Mother of mercy; our life, our sweetness, and our hope, hail. To you do we cry, poor banished children of Eve. To you do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn, then, most gracious advocate, your eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile, show unto us the blessed fruit of your womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

blocks.chantTranslation:
\V. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.//\R. That we may be made worthy
of the promises of Christ. Let us pray.
Almighty and everlasting God, who by the cooperation of the Holy Spirit
prepared the body and soul//of the glorious Virgin Mother Mary
to become a worthy dwelling //for your Son: grant that we
who rejoice in her commemoration//may, by her loving intercession,
be delivered from present evils//and from everlasting death.
Through the same Christ our Lord.// \R. Amen.
\V. May the divine assistance remain always with us. \R. Amen.
